images.title: One square inch in square centimetres
images.purpose: Shows that a square inch, 2.54 cm on each side, holds 6.4516 square centimetres, not 2.54.
images.composition: One large square, centred, divided by a centimetre grid.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A square of side 2.54 units, drawn large, outlined thick dark. Inside, grey (#6B7280) lines at 1 and 2 units from the left and from the bottom divide it into: 4 whole 1 by 1 squares (bottom left 2 by 2 block) filled teal (#0072B2); 4 thin strips, each 1 by 0.54 (2 along the right edge, 2 along the top edge) filled amber (#E69F00); and 1 tiny 0.54 by 0.54 square in the top right corner filled reddish purple (#CC79A7). Labels: 2.54 cm under the bottom side; 2.54 cm beside the left side; 1 cm under the first whole square; 1 in² above the square; and below the figure 2.54 × 2.54 = 6.4516 cm². Check: 4 + 4 × 0.54 + 0.2916 = 4 + 2.16 + 0.2916 = 6.4516.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A square inch is 2.54 cm long and 2.54 cm wide, so it holds 2.54 × 2.54 = 6.4516 cm².
images.description: Shows that a square inch, 2.54 cm on each side, holds 6.4516 square centimetres, not 2.54.
images.context: Matches the worked example: 1 in² = 6.4516 cm². Targets the error of answering 2.54.
images.teaching_notes: Count the 4 whole squares first; the strips and corner make up the rest.

image_decisions.why: The square unit conversion error is cured by seeing the square inch filled with centimetre squares.
